long_biography.plain_text:
Expected to follow his father into funeral service, Alandt worked at Verheyden Funeral Home while studying for a mortuary licence. He instead switched to business and earned a degree from the Detroit Institute of Technology. That change redirected him towards automobile retailing and a career built through acquiring and operating franchised dealerships.

Alandt bought a Ford dealership in Flat Rock in 1994, added a Lincoln-Mercury business in Sterling Heights four years later and opened a Volvo store in Macomb Township. His operating approach emphasised customer service, vehicle delivery and long-term local relationships. He later remained a documented minority owner of multiple Ford and Lincoln dealerships while serving as a director of the charitable foundation he shares with his wife, Lynn.
